newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks end higher on Telecom interest.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks end higher on Telecom interest.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks closed slightly up on Monday, largely on speculative interest in Hongkong Telecom, brokers said.
"If you take out the six percent gain in Hongkong Telecom today, the index would have been down," said Claire Burges-Watson in institutional sales at Kim Eng Securities.

The Hang Seng Index finished 20.70 points up at 12,771.86 after recovering from an 80-point tumble at the start of the day. Turnover remained robust at HK$6.41 billion but was substantially off Friday's HK$8.42 billion.
"It is pure speculative buying. Nobody of any institutional weight is on the board buying (Hongkong Telecom)," Burges-Watson said.
Hongkong Telecom rose HK$0.80 or 6.20 percent to HK$13.70 on turnover of HK$367.18 million.
Most of the market's recent leaders underwent some selling, suggesting the index could see a pullback on Tuesday.
"It should be a quiet day tomorrow. We are overdue for a bit of consolidation," said Lino Delgado, associate director at Amsteel Securities.
Technical analysts said the market had seen good volume on the retracement leg following a downturn in the index.
"We haven't seen such strong buying interest during the retracement period before, said Alice Lee, technical analyst at Tai Fook Securities.
Lee says support lies at 12,600 and near-term resistance at 12,900.

The November Hang Seng Index futures closed unchanged at 12,765, while the December contract which saw a slight increase in volume closed down 15 points at 12,815. Turnover in the November contract was moderate at 12,526.
The utility sector led the market, largely due to the rise in Hongkong Telecom. All other blue chip sectors declined.
The H share sector, came in for especially heavy selling, while red chips, Chinese companies incorporated in Hong Kong but with operations in China, saw strong buying interest.

China Resources Beijing Land was the most actively traded issue of the day. The share eased HK$0.175 to HK$3.875. The share was offered at HK$2.36. Kerry Properties was the day's best performer rising HK$1.05, or 5.34 percent, to HK420.70.
Northeast Electrical led the H shares down, with a fall of HK$0.13 to HK$0.88. -- Kathleen Kearney (852) 2843 6933
